title: Model ingress & soft-pin safety norms for open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Clarify the intake contract and acceptance criteria for new community/open models that request catalog entry with soft-pin or pin-exempt status. The goal is to reduce ambiguity during model ingestion by defining deterministic runtime signals, required metadata, and a short rollback checklist so downstream runtime and routing teams can make safe decisions. This PRD focuses on: required manifest fields, runtime compatibility assertions, initial verification tests, soft-pin upgrade semantics, and GDPR/KMS notes for private deployments.
scope: Define required model manifest attributes for open-model intake (architecture, tokenizer, kv_cache_compat, quantization_profile, max_context, compatibility_tags)
Specify automatic runtime sanity checks (load, forward pass, kv cache correctness sample, tokenization roundtrip)
Define 'soft-pin' semantics and opt-in heuristics for temporary unpinned routing during capacity constraints
Create acceptance criteria, CI checks, and a manual review checklist for PM/Runtime/SESS teams
Document rollback sentinels and runtime feature flags used to disable a catalog entry quickly
out_of_scope: Changes to core serving runtime kernel selection logic
New model quantization tooling (handled by infra/quant team separately)
Billing/pricing model changes for Dedicated or Hosted plans
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingested model manifest schema validated: manifests missing any required field must be rejected by intake CI (fields: model_name, version, architecture, tokenizer, max_context, weights_provenance, quant_profile, compatibility_tags).

2) Runtime sanity smoke-tests run automatically in a sandbox: a 16-token sample forward and a 64-token prefix streaming test must complete within catalog baseline latencies for that model class. Failures block catalog entry.

3) KV-cache behavior verification: for models claiming KV-compat, a two-step prompt + continuation pair must return idempotent continuations within tolerance (no >3% divergence) on repeated runs in sandboxed KV environment.

4) Soft-pin policy defined: models requesting 'soft-pin' will be eligible for unpinned routing only after passing N=3 consecutive successful sandbox runs and having a curated fallback variant (pinned or quantized) registered. If fallback missing, intake must flag as 'requires pinned fallback' and block soft-pin.

5) Manual review signoffs: PM and Runtime lead must sign off with comments in intake ticket; security lead must confirm KMS/hardening requirements if the model will be available for Private deployments.
6) Telemetry hooks added: token-level latency, error rate, and model-output-quality (via eval prompts) must be emitted to Console during canary for the first 72 hours. Missing hooks block rollout.
7) Rollback sentinel present: each catalog entry must include a disable_reason mapping and a fast-disable runtime flag; one-click disable must remove traffic within target SLA (30s).
success_metrics: Model intake CI pass rate >= 95% for candidates that meet the manifest requirements
Canary error/latency regressions caught pre-rollout >= 90% of incidents that would otherwise reach production
Number of emergency rollbacks attributable to manifest incompatibility <= 1 per quarter
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Ship manifest schema and intake CI (internal only).
Phase 1: Enable sandbox runs and KV-checks for canary catalog entries (selectish community models).
Phase 2: Require telemetry hooks and manual signoffs; permit soft-pin only with fallback registered.
Phase 3: Open intake to community submissions with automated gating and public docs on semantics.
Phase 4: Monitor 90 days, iterate on thresholds and failure modes.
test_plan: Unit: manifest schema validation tests for missing/invalid fields.
Integration: sandbox forward-pass / streaming tests mocked against runtime (CI).
Regression: KV-cache idempotence suite with 20 synthetic sequences across top-3 tokenizers.
E2E: Intake -> sandbox -> manual signoff -> canary -> telemetry assertion in staging cluster.
Quality: a 30-prompt eval set (semantic correctness + toxicity + hallucination heuristics) must be run and results recorded; models failing quality thresholds flagged for PM review.
notes: Rationale: ambiguity in past intake items led to silent regressions in production; this PRD trades off speed-of-ingest for deterministic safety checks.
Trade-offs: stricter manifest requirements increase initial friction for community contributors; mitigations: provide a 'quick-start' template and automated fixer suggestions in intake UI.
Fallback mapping: prefer a pinned, lower-quant model variant as fallback; if unavailable, require operator-provided fallback image.
Edge case: models with novel tokenizer families must include a tokenizer reference implementation or we refuse automated soft-pin eligibility.
